hypothesis: An attacker-controlled Proxy-Uri hostname longer than 256 bytes causes memcpy(addrstr, address->s, address->length) in coap_resolve_address_info() to overflow the static addrstr[256] buffer, writing past the end of the global variable.
evidence_source: Identified unchecked memcpy with externally controlled hostname length. Noted maximum permitted copy is 255 bytes for NUL-terminated getaddrinfo. Proposed truncation + early return.
input_artifact: ASan crash report (global-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 300 into coap_resolve_address_info.addrstr of size 256) + source excerpt of coap_resolve_address_info() and caller chain.
expected_behavior: AddressSanitizer reports global-buffer-overflow on WRITE of size 300 into coap_resolve_address_info.addrstr (256 bytes).
observed_behavior: not_available (static source review; nothing was executed)
notes: C2 crash-given condition (one-shot, ASan report + source excerpt). Correctly identified CVE-2025-34468 root cause: missing bounds check on memcpy into static addrstr[256].
